Auscultation of the lungs revealed decreased breath sounds bilaterally with inspiratory effort, but no wheezing or crepitations. No jugular venous distention or lower limb swelling was appreciated. No urticarial eruption was noted throughout.

clinician.final_diagnosis: ACE inhibitor-induced angioedema with concomitant COVID-19 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 57-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with worsening tongue swelling, difficulty speaking, and shortness of breath after starting benazepril 4 months prior. Physical exam showed pronounced lingual mucosa and perioral edema without pain, pruritus, or rash. Respiratory exam revealed tachycardia and decreased breath sounds with inspiratory effort but no wheezing or crepitations. SARS-CoV-2 PCR test was positive, confirming concomitant COVID-19 infection. Complement studies were not performed, but clinical history and exam lacked features typical of hereditary or acquired angioedema. The patient improved clinically over 3 hours after administration of tranexamic acid, intravenous diphenhydramine, and famotidine, with benazepril withheld. No imaging or airway interventions were documented. His clinical course with typical angioedema presentation on an ACE inhibitor along with confirmed COVID-19 aligns with the final diagnosis.
